scope: Eight development fixtures; implementation parity, not corpus retrieval quality

fp32.rationale: Same weights and packed inputs warrant strict agreement. FP32 parallel reduction order is not bit-identical. A 1e-4 unit-coordinate bound and 0.99999 cosine leave margin over historical six-case 1e-6-scale differences; 0.01 absolute on unnormalized activations accommodates accumulation at much larger scales. Every visual/deepstack/pooled tensor is checked. These are regression limits, not a semantic-quality claim.

bf16.rationale: BF16 has approximately 0.008 relative spacing, and output normalization itself is BF16. This is an exploratory numerical bound only; production integration initially selects the strict FP32 reference path.

quantization.rationale: Compare controlled same-source affine 4-bit group64 with FP32 separately from the community artifact. Report query rankings and pairwise score drift; this small fixture set cannot justify corpus retrieval acceptance.

preprocessing.acceptance: integration uses the exact pinned official processor contract audited against Torch
preprocessing.rationale: Token boundaries, timestamps and resize kernels differ; do not use an embedding tolerance to excuse different preprocessing. MLX processor inputs are diagnostic variants only. Single/odd clips explicitly repeat the final frame and its timestamp.

performance.rationale: Report materialized load, first per-shape call and three warm calls; no claim of cold filesystem cache. Intermediate feature extraction is outside latency timing. MLX allocator peak and process high-water RSS include diagnostics and are reported as process-wide peaks, not per-request increments.
